chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakil narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Muthanna, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Do not belittle a poor believer, for whoever belittles a poor believer and treats him lightly, Allah will belittle him and remain his enemy until he ceases from belittling him or repents. He said: And whoever humiliates a believer and belittles him due to his lack of wealth and his poverty, Allah will expose him on the Day of Judgment before all creatures.

key_terms.رُءُوسِ الْخَلَائِقِ: Heads of all creatures (publicly before everyone)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of humiliating a poor believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the spiritual danger of class-based arrogance by linking the humiliation of a poor believer to Allah’s personal enmity (maqit) and public disgrace on the Day of Judgment. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on social equity, warning that financial status is not a measure of spiritual worth, and that belittling the poor invites divine retribution until repentance is made.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakil who said it was narrated to me by Abdillah b. Ja’far al-Himyari from Muhammad b. al-Hussain b. Abi al-Khattab from al-Khattab from al-Hassan b. Mahbub from al-Muthana from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “

Do not insult a poor believer because the Almighty Allah insults one who insults a poor believer. Allah will become his enemy till he does not stop doing so or repents for his deed. One who disgraces a believer because of his poverty the Almighty Allah will disgrace him on the Day of Judgment in front of His entire creation.”
